name: How does a feasibility assessment differ from a general consultation or estimate?

mainEntity.name: How does a feasibility assessment differ from a general consultation or estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: A feasibility assessment is a more in-depth, investigative process compared to a general consultation or preliminary estimate. While a consultation provides an overview of your project and a broad cost range, a feasibility assessment delves into the specific structural, regulatory, and practical details of your property. It proactively identifies potential roadblocks and opportunities, providing a solid foundation for detailed design and accurate budgeting. A general estimate offers a cost projection based on assumptions, whereas a feasibility assessment validates those assumptions, ensuring the project's core concept is viable before proceeding with extensive design work, aligning with our integrated design-build approach.
acceptedAnswer.description: A feasibility assessment is an in-depth investigation of structural and regulatory details, unlike a general consultation or estimate that offers broad overviews or cost projections.
